doc: Ghost-checks catalog (docs/GHOST_CHECKS_PLAN.md). `protocols` — G0 inventory to invariant level; `scopes` — every atomic/ordering site in src/** and crates/*/src/** claimed by exactly one scope (scripts/ghost_inventory.mjs --check); `rules` — per-site lint rules, filled from G1 on.

protocols.name: HeapLease FREE->LIVE claim / LIVE->FREE Release drop
invariants: I1 exactly one thread wins FREE->LIVE for a slot; a losing CAS performs no metadata write, no drain and no drop
I2 every owner write to slot metadata happens-before the next claimant's first read: LIVE->FREE is a Release CAS paired with the claimant's Acquire success ordering
I3 only the lease holder mutates slot metadata between claim and drop
protocols.real_under_loom: no: HeapRegistry is a process-static built through bootstrap::ensure (OncePtrCell + chunked slots); cas_state itself is one CAS on HeapSlot::state and builds alone
protocols.reason: G3: HeapSlot::cas_state only passes the orderings through, so translating it under loom adds nothing; the orderings live at the claim/drop call sites, which need the registry bootstrap. R1 pins every cas_state call site of claim_impl, HeapLease::drop and push_back_after_oom (R4: a lost drop CAS is fatal); R8 binds the drop and claim lines of both shadow models (heap-lease/model-bind, recycle-drain/model-bind). The text pin r11_ph4a_drop_ordering_pinned is removed: its mutants turn heap-lease/drop-release and heap-lease/drop-lost-cas-fatal red.

protocols.name: MaintenanceLease FREE->MAINTENANCE
invariants: I1 a failed FREE->MAINTENANCE CAS never creates a second metadata mutator
I2 MAINTENANCE->FREE is a Release CAS; the next LIVE claimant observes every maintenance write
protocols.real_under_loom: no: same registry bootstrap as P1
protocols.reason: G4: R1 on the FREE -> MAINTENANCE claim (try_maintenance_at) and the MAINTENANCE -> FREE recycle (MaintenanceLease::drop), R4 makes a lost recycle CAS fatal; R8 binds the R8 maintenance model lines to both P2 and P1 rules. The Relaxed-drop mutant is red in the linter and, propagated to the model, a loom causality violation.

protocols.name: publish || recycle || drain (TORN stamp, trim, drop, claimant drain)
invariants: I1 a publication made before, during or after the owner's trim is consumed exactly once (trim or claimant drain) or survives pending for the next owner
I2 trim_for_recycle drains before the LIVE->FREE Release
I3 only the current lease holder drains
protocols.real_under_loom: no: drain runs through HeapCore + AllocCore segment tables
protocols.reason: G3: L1/L2 (R4b-13/14) are caught by the Ph4b model through a core cell every lease holder writes, and by R1 in claim.rs; R8 keeps the model lines equal to prod. The teardown order is R3/R4 on LeaseReleaseGuard::drop and finish_bind, the LOCAL/GUARD declarations are R10. The text pins r11_ph4b_teardown_ordering_pinned and r11_ph4b_local_no_drop_pinned are removed: their mutants turn those rules red. Exactly-once consumption under the real drain is P7/P10 (G6).
protocols.atomics: its orderings are P1 (HeapSlot::cas_state call sites) and P7 (sidecar publish/cut); trim/drain order and consumption are sequence/ghost properties (R3, ghost_event!)

protocols.name: registry claim/selector, free-set, spill, saturation
invariants: I1 count only grows (bump_count CAS) and every slot below count is initialised before it is published (initialised Release / Acquire)
I2 a free-set bit is set only after the slot is FREE (publish Release) and a taker clears it with AcqRel before claiming
I3 the summary word never hides a non-empty word (clear_summary_recheck re-publishes)
I4 saturation is monotone until publish_claimable clears it
protocols.real_under_loom: partial: FreeSlotHint and SaturationHint are self-contained structs on core atomics (translatable via #[path]); stack.rs scans walk the static registry
protocols.reason: G5: free_slot_hint.rs and saturation.rs take their atomics from `super` and run as actual source under loom (tests/loom_registry_hints_actual.rs: no lost or duplicated free-set publication, saturation only after every completed publication); every CAS / RMW of the free set, the saturation hint, bump_count and the hint swaps is pinned by R1, and all five shadow models bind those lines through R8. The stack scans stay shadow models: they walk the process-static registry.

protocols.name: route pin: lookup || unlink || last-pin release
invariants: I1 a pin is taken only under the shard lock while the entry is indexed (refs fetch_update AcqRel)
I2 the sidecar is freed only by the thread whose fetch_sub(AcqRel) returns 1
I3 lookup after remove never yields a pin; linked is cleared with Release before unlink
I4 Block/BlockIndex/spare atomics are Relaxed and touched only under the shard lock
protocols.real_under_loom: yes: tests/loom_b4_r1_pin_cache.rs includes directory/ and src/ghost/
protocols.decision: translate (done in G2: real directory under loom via loom_b4_r1_pin_cache with ghost checks compiled in; last-reference free under miri)
protocols.reason: pilot: correctness item 186

protocols.name: route pin cache fast path
invariants: I1 a cached pin is reused only while it holds its own ref; eviction drops exactly one ref
I2 the cache is thread-local; no cross-thread access
protocols.real_under_loom: yes (already #[path])
protocols.reason: G6b: the real cache records ghost event pin-cache/held (+1 when a pin enters a slot, -1 when it leaves) keyed by segment base; the actual-source loom model checks the ledger against Entry::refs (one reference per occupied slot; 0 after the unlink fallback and after the TLS destructor). R6 with counts keeps every event per fn; R10 pins both cfg twins of CACHE as thread_local RefCell<PinCache>; R4/R5 keep inserts on the non-fallback slow path.
protocols.atomics: the cache is thread-local; the only cross-thread word it touches is P5's Entry::refs through EntryHandle (its own atomics are counters)

protocols.name: sidecar bitmap: publish / guarded cut / scan
invariants: I1 every published offset is cut exactly once
I2 publish is fetch_or AcqRel after the class store Release; cut is swap AcqRel
protocols.real_under_loom: yes (loom_sidecar_bitmap_actual.rs)
protocols.reason: G6a: ghost events sidecar/published (publish) and sidecar/cut-bits (next_cut), checked by a per-word ledger in the actual-source loom test (every publication cut exactly once); R1 on the publish fetch_or, the issue store and the three cut swaps; R6 keeps both events. The text pin r11_ph5b_c5 is removed (its R5b-13/R5b-14 mutants turn sidecar/publish-acqrel and sidecar/cut-acqrel red). Retiring the shadow loom_sidecar_bitmap.rs moves to G6c with the P8 translation (R0-21 still cites it).

protocols.name: small sidecar: leaf pointer publication, pin lifetime
invariants: I1 a leaf pointer is published (mixed store Release, present fetch_or Release) only after the leaf is fully initialised
I2 a reader resolves a leaf only with Acquire and only while holding a route pin
protocols.real_under_loom: partial: ClassLeaves allocates leaves through the OS seam (cfg(loom) twin, P18)
protocols.reason: G6a: ClassLeaves ordered-op inventory per fn (R2 x6), initialise-before-publish and publish-before-presence in promote (R3), Drop walks presence bits (R3); R5 forbids the Dense constructor in production and keeps from_leaves in SmallSidecar::bitmap. Translation of the small-sidecar model follows in G6c.

protocols.name: terminal Large: phase word
invariants: I1 the phase word moves only along the transition relation (kani large_state_proofs)
I2 every transition CAS is AcqRel/Acquire; a terminal publication is the producer's last reservation access
protocols.real_under_loom: yes: tests/loom_terminal_large.rs compiles reservation_state.rs and terminal_words.rs onto loom atomics
protocols.reason: G6c: tests/loom_terminal_large.rs now runs the production LargeReservationState and phase codec on loom atomics (reservation_state.rs takes its atomics from super); ghost event large/pending (+1 publish, -1 claim) checked by a per-word ledger; R2 x5 exact ordered-op tables, R4 x3 phase checks before each observed-word CAS, R6 x2 on the events.

protocols.name: terminal owner drain: owner credits || cut
invariants: I1 credits are mutated only by the owner (plain fields, no atomics)
I2 a terminal cut consumes each pending bit once
protocols.real_under_loom: no: credits live in AllocCore
protocols.reason: G6b: credits stay a plain owner-only u32 (R10 on SegmentHeader.live_count); R5 pins every credit mutator (set_live_count, add_live, inc_live, sub_live, dec_live) to its owner functions; R4 keeps the drain release inside the empty-segment check; the shadow model binds the publish and cut orderings to P7 (R8).
protocols.atomics: owner credits are plain fields of AllocCore; the cut is P7's BitmapScan::next_cut swap

protocols.name: active-kind index membership || terminal publication
invariants: I1 the owner alone owns the membership bit (plain)
I2 a segment is removed from the active-kind index only after its pending credit is consumed or it is reservation-dead
protocols.real_under_loom: no: index is part of SegmentTable
protocols.reason: G6b: membership words stay plain owner u64s (R10); R5 pins ActiveKindIndex::set/clear to register/unregister/recycle; R3 (nested_before) keeps every cut consumed before finish_small_drain in all three owner drains; the shadow model binds the publish and cut orderings to P7 (R8).
protocols.atomics: membership is a plain owner bit in SegmentTable; producer side is P7's pending fetch_or

protocols.name: depot across slot recycle
invariants: I1 the depot is empty at LIVE->FREE (drained in trim_for_recycle before the Release)
I2 only the current lease holder touches the depot
protocols.real_under_loom: no: owner-only plain storage bound as &'static mut
protocols.reason: G4: no atomics of its own. R3 depot/flush-reloads-parked keeps the teardown flush draining every parked magazine; R5 depot/owner-only-access and depot/bind-once keep the depot reachable only through the owner paths and bound once; the drain-before-Release order is G3 teardown/trim-before-release, which the depot model now binds as an R8 step together with the drop/claim orderings.
protocols.atomics: the depot is plain owner-only storage; its cross-thread safety is P1's LIVE->FREE Release / claim Acquire

rules.reason: plan §3.1/§4.2 R9: no ghost fields in prod structs, ghost macro arguments never write, ghost:: paths outside the macros only under a ghost cfg
the last dropper must observe every other holder's accesses before it frees the Entry and sidecar: Release on every decrement, Acquire on the final one
a pin increment is a counted reference the final decrement synchronizes with
the unlink is published with Release; RoutePin::linked reads it with Acquire (cached fast path gate)
the sidecar is freed only after the early return of every non-final decrement (item 186)
free_sidecar is dominated by the reference decrement in the same or an enclosing block
only the last reference (or the constructor's own OOM rollback) frees a sidecar
the drop keeps its ghost underflow check (and the freed-once event the harness counts)
the pin keeps its ghost no-resurrection check (item 186)
the shadow model of item 186 keeps the production orderings of the decrement and the unlink
S2: every owner write to the core happens-before the next claimant; the LIVE -> FREE CAS is the Release half of that edge
a lost LIVE -> FREE CAS means a second mutator exists; the drop aborts instead of continuing
the claimant's FREE -> LIVE success ordering is the Acquire half of S2: it observes every write of the previous holder
exactly one first claimant wins EMPTY -> INITIALIZING and becomes the sole constructor of the core
a FREE slot whose core was never published is re-entered as INITIALIZING by the winner that already holds it
the constructed core is published with the LIVE state after the initialised Release store
a failed construction hands the slot back as FREE with Release; the next claimant reads initialised before choosing a path
the Ph4a shadow model keeps the production orderings of the drop and claim CAS
the Ph4b shadow model keeps the production orderings of the drop and claim CAS; its core cell makes a weakened one a loom causality violation (R4b-13/R4b-14)
LOCAL is poisoned before any owner-side mutation of the teardown, so a later resolver never aliases the next claimant
every release of the slot (early process-exit or terminal) follows the TORN stamp
the terminal sidecar cut and cache trim run while this thread is still the sole owner; no core mutation after LIVE -> FREE
the only release that skips the trim is the process-exit early return
the GUARD-arming rollback un-publishes LOCAL before it releases the slot, so no stale published pointer outlives the lease
owner decision "LOCAL without Drop": a const-initialised raw Cell registers no destructor, stays readable for the TORN stamp and has no borrow state
the guard moves the lease out with take(), so the LIVE -> FREE CAS runs exactly once at the explicit drop
the maintenance taker wins FREE -> MAINTENANCE once and acquires every write of the previous holder; a failed CAS creates no second mutator
MAINTENANCE -> FREE publishes every maintenance write with Release to the next LIVE claimant
a lost MAINTENANCE -> FREE CAS means a second mutator exists; the drop aborts
the R8 maintenance model keeps the production claim and recycle orderings of both the LIVE and the MAINTENANCE lease
the teardown flush reloads every parked magazine into the emptied magazine and flushes it too, so the depot is empty at LIVE -> FREE

I3: after clearing a summary bit the word is re-read and a non-empty word is re-published, so the summary never hides a published bit
a claimant that took the slot another way withdraws its bit with AcqRel
